rule: A definition that a guest can bind must not do nothing. A guest dispatches a public symbol by name, and an exported weak definition or an exported placeholder body still satisfies that binding, so the real implementation elsewhere is never reached. This was measured on 2026-10-10 (ADR-0004): libsystem_kernel exported os_unfair_lock_lock/os_unfair_lock_unlock as empty weak functions, every guest os_unfair_lock became a no-op, and exclusion failed 2798 of 2800 rounds. Every definition in this forest that has that shape is therefore a candidate that must be classified here: weak linkage, or a placeholder body behind explicit default visibility under a name a guest could bind. An addition the contract cannot find a classification for fails it by name, and a classification whose anchored source digest moved fails it until it is reviewed again. Every entry also records whether the image DEFINES the name or merely IMPORTS it (image_role), because the fix for this class flips exactly that: a weak definition a guest could bind becomes a weak import the caller tests for NULL, and a retired entry then says what the removal left behind.

scan.weak_import_grammar: A name counts as imported when the anchored source declares it with __attribute__((weak_import)) or with a macro the forest defines as exactly that attribute (the emulation's WEAK_IMPORT, weak_import on the Darwin targets and plain weak on the ELF side).
scan.candidate_rule: A candidate is a file-scope, non-static definition with a body that is (a) weak-attributed, whatever its visibility, or (b) explicitly default-visible and wholly a placeholder body. Visibility is not considered on the weak arm because the measured instance carried no visibility attribute and still won a guest binding; the placeholder arm requires explicit default visibility because these libraries compile with -fvisibility=hidden, so an unmarked placeholder cannot reach the export table. Preprocessor directives, comments, string contents and the C++ exception specifications that trail a parameter list are not part of the grammar: the scan reads structural source with comments blanked, keeps a string-preserving copy so visibility("default") stays readable, and steps back over throw()/noexcept() before it names the declaration. A definition that is explicitly hidden is not a candidate: ADR-0004's remedy is exactly a private placeholder, and a hidden definition cannot be in the export table. That exclusion is not extended to the weak arm, which stays visibility-agnostic for the measured reason above.

counting.candidate_count: candidates the scan grammar discovers over the source forest; every one of them must have a classification
counting.classified_count: entries with status classified, which must equal candidate_count: an unclassified candidate is refused, not counted
counting.retired_count: entries with status retired, so that a removal is a fact in the registry with the commit that removed it rather than an absence nobody can see

entries.name: os_unfair_lock_lock
entries.caller_dependency: The measured ADR-0004 instance. A guest process dispatches os_unfair_lock_lock by name and this library defined it twice as an empty function, so the guest bound a no-op and libsystem_platform's correct implementation was never reached: a shared unfair lock admitted every thread (2798 of 2800 rounds). The file it lived in still exists and still carries the emulation's own saved-reference lock, now a private libsimple_lock_t, so the definition must stay gone here and this entry keeps that fact reviewable.

retirement.note: libsystem_kernel: stop shadowing the public os_unfair_lock, give the emulation a private lock. The two no-ops in this file were removed and g_savedRefLock moved to libsimple_lock_t, with a prefork hook in include/common/fork_locks.h so a fork cannot snapshot the real lock held.

entries.name: os_unfair_lock_unlock
entries.caller_dependency: The measured ADR-0004 instance, the unlock half of the same pair: with both definitions empty the lock neither excluded nor released anything. The same commit removed it, and the emulation's saved-reference lock is now a private libsimple_lock_t in this file.

retirement.note: libsystem_kernel: stop shadowing the public os_unfair_lock, give the emulation a private lock. Removed together with the lock half and with the pair in workq_kernreturn.c; the private lock is released through darling_savedref_bookkeeping_prefork_release in fork.c.

entries.name: voucher_mach_msg_adopt
entries.caller_dependency: The XNU Mach voucher protocol: the mach_msg send and receive paths adopt a voucher from a message header. This definition returns NULL and the UNIMPLEMENTED_TRAP that would have reported the gap is commented out, so a guest that binds it gets no voucher accounting at all and nothing says so. No strong side exists anywhere in this forest.

entries.name: voucher_mach_msg_revert
entries.caller_dependency: The XNU Mach voucher protocol: the caller reverts the voucher after the message is handled. This definition returns nothing at all and the UNIMPLEMENTED_TRAP is commented out, so the revert is a silent no-op. No strong side exists anywhere in this forest.

entries.name: voucher_mach_msg_set
entries.caller_dependency: The XNU Mach voucher protocol: the send path asks for the current voucher to attach to a message. This definition returns 0, which reads as "no voucher to set", and the UNIMPLEMENTED_TRAP is commented out, so the guest silently sends messages without voucher attribution. No strong side exists anywhere in this forest.

entries.name: os_unfair_lock_lock
entries.caller_dependency: The second of the two files that exported the public os_unfair_lock as an empty weak function: this one satisfied the same guest binding from the workqueue code. The parked-workqueue lock here is now a private libsimple_lock_t, so the public name is defined nowhere in this layer.

retirement.note: libsystem_kernel: stop shadowing the public os_unfair_lock, give the emulation a private lock. workq_parked_lock moved to libsimple_lock_t and fork.c takes it before the fork through darling_workq_bookkeeping_prefork_prepare.

entries.name: os_unfair_lock_unlock
entries.caller_dependency: The unlock half of the second pair. The commit that removed it is the one the ADR evidence names (xnu 95588ba on fix/private-ulock-return-channel), and the guest's lock image was measured afterwards as libsystem_platform.dylib with zero exclusion violations of 2800 rounds.

retirement.note: libsystem_kernel: stop shadowing the public os_unfair_lock, give the emulation a private lock. Removed together with the lock half; release goes through darling_workq_bookkeeping_prefork_release.

entries.name: kevent_impl
entries.caller_dependency: sys_kevent calls it with the guest's changelist. No definition remains in the dylib; the caller holds a weak import tested for NULL and libkqueue supplies the strong definition (measured: kevent -> 0).

retirement.note: libsystem_kernel: stop defining the kqueue hooks, import them weakly instead. No definition remains in libsystem_kernel.dylib: the callers hold weak imports and test them for NULL, and the linker records libsystem_c as the expected provider (libkqueue, which carries the strong definitions). The loader archives (libsystem_kernel_static32/64.a, the VARIANT_DYLD branch of each source) keep HIDDEN definitions because an undefined weak reference there is a hard link error (measured: "ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture i386"); those are private externals and cannot satisfy a guest dynamic binding. Measured on this commit: the guest weak-binding audit passes (kqueue() -> fd, kevent -> 0, close -> 0, dup(0) -> fd, the loud fallback absent), doctor healthy 0 problems / 76 passed, and the T4 toolchain gate PASS.
